known_facts_book1: A wooden-limbed man with a carved pumpkin head, built and dressed by Tip and brought to life by Mombi's Powder of Life.
Wears purple trousers, a red shirt and a pink spotted vest taken from Mombi's chest; his face is carved into a permanent smile.
Calls Tip his father and parent and owes him obedience while Tip owes him support.
Lives in constant terror of spoiling (rotting), especially from water, heat, or old age.
Rides the Saw-Horse because his wooden joints wear out from walking.
Loses his pumpkin head in the river and again in a rabbit hole; it is retrieved and replaced each time.
Has his left leg amputated by the Tin Woodman to mend the Saw-Horse, and later gets a carved mahogany table-leg.
Wrongly assumes he speaks a separate 'Pumpkinhead' language, until Jellia Jamb reveals only one tongue is spoken in all Oz.
Remains with Queen Ozma to the end of his days, never spoiling as soon as he feared but staying as stupid as ever.

known_relations_book1.Tip: His maker, whom he calls 'father'; when Tip becomes the girl Ozma the fatherhood ends and Jack is not sorry to escape it.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Fellow artificial being who befriends him at the palace.
known_relations_book1.Saw-Horse: His steed and frequent quarrel-partner; Jack's amputated leg becomes the Saw-Horse's new leg.
known_relations_book1.Nick Chopper: The Tin Woodman, who catches his falling head and carves him new legs.
known_relations_book1.Woggle-Bug: Suggests using Jack's leg for the Saw-Horse; later tries and fails to educate him.

known_facts_book1: Ruler of the Emerald City, made King by its people after the Wizard fled; a straw-stuffed man with a painted sack head and prized brains from the Wizard.
Dethroned by General Jinjur's Army of Revolt, which conquers the city while he plays quoits.
Escapes with Tip and Jack on the Saw-Horse, all tied together, and flees to his friend the Tin Woodman.
Hides twelve field mice in his straw; releasing them stampedes Jinjur's army out of the throne room.
Conceives the plan to escape Jinjur's palace by air, having the Tin Woodman build the Gump.
Is stuffed with banknotes stolen by the Jackdaws after the birds carry off his straw, becoming 'the richest man in the world.'
Willingly yields the throne once he learns the rightful heir Ozma still lives.
Is made Royal Treasurer by the Tin Woodman at the end and resolves never to be parted from him.
Prizes his brains above all, and repeatedly stops to 'take time to think.'

known_relations_book1.Nick Chopper: The Tin Woodman, his oldest and dearest friend; flees to him, is restored to the throne by him, and at the end is made his Royal Treasurer, the two vowing never to part.
known_relations_book1.Jinjur: The rebel who dethrones him and usurps his crown.
known_relations_book1.Tip: Befriends the boy and, after the reveal, pats him and stays his faithful friend.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Sorceress he appeals to for help, who reveals the true heir Ozma.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The rightful heir he gladly steps aside for; he had held the crown only since the Wizard passed it to him.

known_facts_book1: Emperor of the Winkies (the yellow West country), who prefers 'Emperor' to 'King'; his real name is Nick Chopper.
Made entirely of tin and newly nickel-plated so he shines; wears an engraved star over the heart the Wizard gave him.
The Scarecrow's oldest friend; shelters him and resolves to restore his throne.
Fights off the Jackdaws with his axe and frightens Jinjur's guards with its whirling sweep.
Builds the Gump flying machine from two sofas, palm-leaf wings, a mounted Gump's head, and a broom tail.
Unwittingly captures Mombi by plucking the red rose (her transformed shape) and wearing it in his tin buttonhole.
Values his kind heart above brains or education.
At the end makes the Scarecrow his Royal Treasurer and invites Ozma to visit his Winkie kingdom.

known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: His dearest friend, whom he shelters, restores to the throne, and makes Royal Treasurer, vowing never to part.
known_relations_book1.Queen of the Field Mice: An old friend whose life he once saved; he summons her with a silver whistle for aid.
known_relations_book1.Tip: Befriends the boy and comforts him about becoming a girl.
known_relations_book1.Mombi: Unknowingly carries her out of the city as a rose in his buttonhole.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Sorceress he and the Scarecrow know and turn to for help.

known_facts_book1: A once-ordinary insect who lived for years in Professor Nowitall's schoolhouse hearth, absorbing the lessons.
Caught and thrown upon a screen 'highly magnified,' he escaped while still enlarged; 'H. M.' means Highly Magnified.
'T. E.' means Thoroughly Educated; he prides himself on learning and endless puns that annoy his companions.
Dressed by a tailor whose ninth life he saved; wears a swallowtail coat, vest, knickerbockers and a tall silk hat.
Joins the party on the road to the Emerald City and suggests using Jack's leg to mend the Saw-Horse.
Swallows a Wishing Pill without pain and wishes the Gump's broken wings mended.
Is appointed Public Educator to Queen Ozma at the end and tries, in vain, to educate Jack.

known_relations_book1.Professor Nowitall: The schoolmaster in whose classroom he was educated and magnified.
known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Travelling companion who tolerates but tires of his puns.
known_relations_book1.Nick Chopper: The Tin Woodman, a travelling companion who twice threatens him with the axe over his jokes.
known_relations_book1.Tip: Companion who curbs his puns; the Woggle-Bug offers to tutor Tip once he becomes a girl.

known_facts_book1: A wooden sawbuck brought to life by Tip with the Powder of Life; it has knot eyes, a branch for a tail, and no knee-joints.
Cannot hear until Tip whittles and fits bark ears on it; it rocks side to side 'like a cradle' as it paces.
Carries Jack Pumpkinhead, and bolts and races ahead, separating from Tip on the road.
Breaks a leg in a rabbit hole and is given one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs as a replacement.
Carries Glinda in the chase and outruns Mombi's Griffin form across the desert, forcing her capture.
Becomes Queen Ozma's personal property; she has its wooden legs shod with gold.

known_relations_book1.Tip: Brought to life by Tip; on the reveal it becomes Ozma's personal steed, shod with gold.
known_relations_book1.Jack Pumpkinhead: Carries him and quarrels with him; wears one of Jack's amputated legs.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: Carries the Sorceress in the pursuit that runs down and captures Mombi.

known_facts_book1: Originally only a mounted Gump's head, like an elk's, hung over the palace mantel; the Woggle-Bug fetches it for the flying machine.
The Gump is a Thing built of two sofas, four palm-leaf wings, the Gump's head as figure-head, and a broom for a tail, brought to life when Tip sprinkles the Powder of Life on its head.
Only its head is alive; its sofa legs are not, so it flies but cannot walk.
Carries the party south, is blown off course to the outside world, and crashes on a mountain, breaking its right wings.
Its broken wings are mended by the Woggle-Bug's Wishing-Pill wish.
At its own request Ozma has it taken apart; the talking head is re-hung over the mantel and keeps startling visitors.

known_relations_book1.Tip: Brought to life by Tip with the last of the Powder of Life.
known_relations_book1.Nick Chopper: The Tin Woodman built its body; the Gump serves the party as an aircraft.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: Grants its wish to be dispersed after it has carried the party to victory.
